known.evidence: Discusses get_prep_lookup only in terms of plain values being wrapped as Value(v, lhs.output_field) instead of only str; never mentions that self.rhs is iterated twice or that a generator gets used up.

other.summary: Related-field __in lists mixing an expression with model instances or pks could fail because ForeignKey.get_db_prep_value may not accept a model instance
other.reason: RelatedIn.get_prep_lookup turns model instances into pks (get_normalized_value) before calling super(), and Value.as_sql runs get_db_prep_value, which calls get_prep_value, so behaviour is equivalent.

other.summary: JSONIn.process_lhs wraps a top-level LHS in JSON_EXTRACT/CASE/COALESCE even when the RHS is a subquery or column, changing comparison semantics for json_field__in=Model.objects.values('json_field')
other.reason: process_lhs wraps every non-KeyTransform LHS while a Query RHS stays raw; in sqlite3, CASE/JSON_EXTRACT(v) IN (select v ...) fails for objects, arrays and strings that matched with the old raw comparison.
Self-described as harmless; only the container type changes.

other.summary: JSONNull detection in as_oracle relies on Value equality and a bare None becomes Value(None, JSONField)
other.reason: Expression equality is based on constructor arguments, so JSONNull() matches correctly; the None part is a request to confirm intent, not a demonstrated defect.

known.evidence: Explicitly says of the get_prep_lookup change: 'I found no regression from this.' Never mentions the double iteration of self.rhs.

other.summary: JSONIn.as_oracle returns '(a) OR (b)' without outer parentheses, so in an AND WhereNode it becomes '(a) OR (b) AND other = 1' and returns wrong rows
other.reason: as_oracle returns ' OR '.join(sql_parts) unwrapped; WhereNode.as_sql joins children with ' AND ' and only wraps the whole node when negated or it has more than one child.

other.summary: Value(JSONNull(), JSONField()) in the list isn't detected by the JSONNull() check in as_oracle
other.reason: Contrived construction (JSONNull is already a Value), and the review itself marks it as an unrun edge case; no realistic use shown.

known.evidence: Its get_prep_lookup note is about reading self.lhs.output_field for non-string items, not about self.rhs being consumed by any() before the second iteration.

other.summary: Oracle JSONIn.as_oracle OR expansion has no outer parentheses, so AND-combined filters return wrong rows
other.reason: Confirmed in json.py as_oracle (unwrapped ' OR '.join) and where.py WhereNode.as_sql (children joined without per-child parentheses).

other.summary: Top-level value__in with a subquery or column RHS wraps only the LHS (JSON_EXTRACT/CASE), so SQLite/MySQL comparisons stop matching
other.reason: process_lhs wraps every non-KeyTransform LHS; a Query RHS bypasses resolve_expression_parameter; sqlite3 check shows objects, arrays and strings no longer match while they did with the raw comparison.

other.summary: get_prep_lookup now reads lhs.output_field for non-string items and could raise FieldError when it can't be resolved
other.reason: The old code already evaluated hasattr(self.lhs, 'output_field'), which doesn't swallow FieldError, and build_lookup must resolve lhs.output_field to find the lookup at all, so the case is unreachable.
